annotations.title: utilpeek: topic trends over time from public attention (Wikipedia views, Hacker News, news), not Google Trends

description: utilpeek: Use when an agent must tell if interest in a topic is rising or fading: Wikipedia, Hacker News and news over time. For the articles use news_search. Returns daily topic trends for 1 to 5 topics: Wikipedia page views per language, Hacker News counts, news mentions, with 7- and 28-day change, spike days, direction and share. Not Google Trends data. Public attention signals, not Google Trends or search volume. `related`: related Wikipedia topics ranked by page views; not search queries and not Google Trends data. Topic = top English Wikipedia hit (see `article.title`). Complete days to yesterday; news only for the last 14 days. Cached 6 h. Bad input is a 422 and an upstream failure a 503 or 504 (not charged). Typically 3 to 15 s (first call for a topic; cached for 6 hours). Price: USD 0.005. Free: 10 utilpeek calls per IP per UTC day. Docs: https://tanod.dev/learn/topic-trends-attention-api.html

end.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), at most yesterday (later is clamped to it). Default: yesterday. The range is at most 365 days.

languages.description: Wikipedia language codes, at most 6 (en, de, ja ...). Default: en plus the four most-read languages that have the article. A language without the article is listed under `languages_skipped`.

related.description: Default false. True (one topic only) adds `related`: up to 10 `top` and 10 `rising` related Wikipedia topics, ranked by page views; not search queries and not Google Trends data.

start.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). Default: 90 days ending at `end`.

topics.description: 1 to 5 topics (words or a name, up to 100 characters each). Each is resolved to the top English Wikipedia search hit, reported as `article.title`. Several topics are compared: each gets its relative share.

name: get_topic_trends_attention

error.description: Only on an error result: an object {code, message}, or the reason string of an x402 PaymentRequired object.
